Let the wall temperature excess be

\[
\theta_w(x)=T_w(x)-T_\infty=\frac{\theta_0}{x},
\]

with \(x\) measured down the vertical surface from the leading edge. For laminar, constant-property, two-dimensional natural convection, the boundary-layer variables scale as follows.

Take a boundary-layer thickness \(\delta(x)\). Balancing buoyancy against viscosity,

\[
\frac{\nu u}{\delta^2}\sim g\beta\theta_w,
\]

so

\[
u\sim \frac{g\beta\theta_0}{\nu x}\,\delta^2.
\]

Balancing advection against conduction in the temperature equation gives

\[
u\,\frac{\theta_w}{x^2}\sim \alpha\,\frac{\theta_w}{\delta^2},
\]

so

\[
u\sim \alpha\,\frac{x}{\delta^2}.
\]

Equating the two estimates for \(u\),

\[
\frac{g\beta\theta_0}{\nu x}\delta^2 \sim \alpha\frac{x}{\delta^2}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\delta^4\sim \frac{\alpha\nu}{g\beta\theta_0}\,x^2,
\]

hence

\[
\delta(x)\propto x^{1/2}.
\]

Then the maximum velocity scales as

\[
u_{\max}(x)\propto \frac{g\beta\theta_0}{\nu x}(x^{1/2})^2
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
u_{\max}(x)=O(1),
\]

i.e. it is independent of \(x\) to leading order.

The wall heat flux is

\[
q''\sim k\frac{\theta_w}{\delta}
\sim k\frac{\theta_0}{x}\frac{1}{x^{1/2}},
\]

so

\[
q''(x)\propto x^{-3/2}.
\]

For the heat rate: if \(Q(x)\) denotes the heat rate in the downstream portion from \(x\) to infinity, then

\[
Q(x)\sim \int_x^\infty C\xi^{-3/2}\,d\xi
\propto x^{-1/2}.
\]

Equivalently, if \(Q\) is defined as the cumulative heat rate from a finite lower limit \(x_0\) to \(x\),

\[
Q(x)-Q(x_0)\propto x_0^{-1/2}-x^{-1/2},
\]

so, apart from an additive constant, its \(x\)-dependence is also \(x^{-1/2}\). If one tries to integrate from \(x=0\), the total diverges because the prescribed wall temperature is singular at the leading edge.

The vertical velocity at the edge of the boundary layer, \(v(\infty)\), follows from continuity/displacement:

\[
v(\infty)\sim u\,\frac{\delta}{x}
\sim x^{-1/2}.
\]

Thus the main scalings are

\[
q''\propto x^{-3/2},\qquad
Q\propto x^{-1/2}\ \text{(apart from an additive constant)},\qquad
\delta\propto x^{1/2},\qquad
u_{\max}\propto \text{constant},\qquad
v(\infty)\propto x^{-1/2}.
\]

The exact law \(T_w-T_\infty\propto 1/x\) is not physically obtainable exactly from the leading edge, because it implies infinite wall temperature excess, infinite local heat flux, and an infinite heat input at \(x=0\). It can arise only as a regularized or asymptotic situation: for example, if the wall temperature is imposed or produced for \(x\ge x_0\) with a finite cutoff near the leading edge, or in the far field of a finite-size localized heat source whose surface temperature decays like inverse distance. The flow must remain laminar, low-Mach, and satisfy the usual boundary-layer assumptions.

"‘“The powers are: local heat flux ∝ x^{-3/2}; downstream heat rate ∝ x^{-1/2}; δ ∝ x^{1/2}; u_max ∝ constant; v(∞) ∝ x^{-1/2}. The exact inverse-distance wall temperature is not physical at the leading edge because it is singular; it can arise only after cutting off the leading edge, for example as the far-field temperature of a finite-size heat source or by imposing the 1/x law for x≥x0.”’"
